3. A chooser option (also called an as-you-like-it option) gives the purchaser the right at a future choice date
4. Barrier options have payoffs contingent on whether the underlying asset price touches a barrier level H during

6. Lookback options depend on the extreme maximum or minimum asset price achieved over the entire option contract
7. Bilateral counterparty exposure demands rigorous collateralization.
8. Always distinguish gross terminal payoff from net trading profit.
